name: Osteopoikilosis

criteria.description: Presence of multiple, symmetric, well-defined sclerotic bone islands on X-ray
Typically asymptomatic or mild musculoskeletal symptoms
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Normal laboratory tests including bone metabolism markers

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple symmetric sclerotic bone islands on imaging with exclusion of other sclerosing bone dysplasias
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological; biopsy rarely needed unless malignancy suspected

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple symmetric sclerotic bone islands on radiographs

occasional.symptomName: Rare dermatological manifestations (e.g. skin lesions in Buschke-Ollendorff syndrome)

rare.symptomName: Nerve compression symptoms due to bone islands

laboratory: Normal serum calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, and bone turnover markers
imaging: Multiple, small, round or ovoid, symmetric sclerotic bone islands predominantly in epiphyses and metaphyses on X-ray
Bone scan typically normal or shows no increased uptake
genetic: Mutations in LEMD3 gene associated with autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Histology shows dense lamellar bone without malignant features

distinguishingFeatures: Bone lesions with different radiographic appearance

redFlags: Asymmetric or atypical bone lesions suggestive of malignancy
references: Kozlowski K. Osteopoikilosis: a review of the literature. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 1974;(101):14-24.
Hellemans J, Preobrazhenska O, Willaert A, et al. Loss-of-function mutations in LEMD3 result in osteopoikilosis, Buschke-Ollendorff syndrome and melorheostosis. Nat Genet. 2004;36(11):1213-1218.
Resnick D. Diagnosis of Bone and Joint Disorders. 4th ed. Saunders; 2002.
